steps.thought: List all available tests to understand station capabilities and select the cheapest tests for initial triage.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly verify overall subsystem enumeration and check for basic communication or component failures across the unit.
steps.observation: The power on selftest passed successfully, enumerating all expected I2C, UART, and CAN devices without any bus errors.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial boot and device enumeration passed, though further subsystem tests are needed to confirm.
I2C devices enumerated properly, but IMU calibration or sensor issues require dedicated IMU testing to rule out.
CAN nodes found, but motor/ESC performance under load must be verified.
Unit powered on normally, but battery resting and load characteristics are still unchecked.
Camera control UART device found, but camera image stream and ribbon integrity need verification.

steps.thought: I will run the battery_rest_check to verify cell voltages and pack rest status cheaply before running more intensive tests.
steps.observation: The battery rest check passed successfully, showing normal pack voltage (16.60V) and very low cell imbalance (0.01V). This rules out dead or weak battery cells.

hypotheses.rationale: Both power-on selftest and battery rest check passed with no failures.
I2C IMU was detected, but its calibration and performance under static conditions remain untested.
CAN nodes enumerated, but motor and ESC telemetry under active conditions still need to be verified.
UART camera control responded, but CSI frame rate and ribbon integrity require dedicated testing.
Compass was detected via I2C, but static heading and motor interference tests are required to check for magnetic anomalies.

steps.thought: I will run the esc_telemetry test to check for any commutation sync errors or packet loss across the ESCs, which is a cheap and direct way to evaluate motor and ESC health.
steps.observation: ESC telemetry passed overall, though esc_3 shows a minor sync error count of 1.0 and 0.17 percent packet loss, which warrants a check but does not indicate a hard fault yet.

hypotheses.rationale: All performed tests (power_on_selftest, battery_rest_check, esc_telemetry) have passed with no critical failures.
ESC_3 reported a sync error and packet loss, suggesting possible commutation or communication issues on this channel.
I2C IMU was detected, but static noise and calibration remain to be tested.
Camera control UART responded, but CSI frame rate and ribbon integrity are still untested.
Compass was detected via I2C, but static heading and motor interference tests are required.

steps.thought: Run harness_continuity to check CAN bus termination and per-bus continuity resistance, ensuring the CAN bus and harness are healthy.
steps.observation: The harness continuity test passed completely, measuring normal bus resistance and a proper CAN termination of 59.8 ohms (representing a parallel 120 ohm pair). This rules out missing CAN terminators, damaged stubs, or open I2C/UART/CAN buses.

hypotheses.rationale: System enumeration, battery rest, ESC telemetry, and harness continuity have all passed without hard failures.
ESC_3 showed a minor sync error count and packet loss during ESC telemetry, requiring a dynamic motor spin test to confirm.
I2C IMU is present and connected, but static noise and sensor bias remain unverified.
Camera UART control responded, but CSI frame rate and ribbon integrity are still untested.
Compass is enumerated on I2C, but static heading and motor interference tests are pending.

steps.thought: Run motor_spin_test to check for any physical motor anomalies, bearing issues, or ESC commutation problems on motor_3.
steps.observation: The motor spin test passed with all motors showing normal current, temperature, RPM, and low jitter, ruling out hard motor or ESC desync faults. With system enumeration, battery rest, ESC telemetry, harness continuity, and motor spin all verified, remaining open items are the camera, IMU, and compass subsystems.

hypotheses.rationale: All power, battery, harness, ESC, and motor tests have passed without failures.
I2C IMU enumerated successfully, but static noise, bias, and calibration remain unverified.
Camera control UART responded, but camera selftest has not yet been executed.
Compass is present on I2C, but static heading and motor interference checks are pending.

steps.thought: Run the camera_selftest to verify camera frame rate, CSI errors, and rule out camera ribbon or sensor faults.
steps.observation: The camera selftest failed with 258 CSI CRC errors and a low frame rate of 20.8 fps, while sensor ID and power-on enumeration passed. This pinpoints a high-speed communication issue between the camera module and flight controller, pointing specifically to a ribbon cable fault rather than a dead sensor or firmware mismatch.

hypotheses.rationale: High CSI CRC errors and reduced frame rate with a responsive camera sensor ID strongly indicate a compromised CSI ribbon cable connection or signal integrity.
Sensor ID passed and the camera boots over UART/I2C, making a completely dead sensor unlikely but possible if the internal video pipeline is damaged.
Firmware mismatch could theoretically cause low frame rates, but CRC errors point primarily to physical layer/ribbon integrity.

steps.thought: The camera subsystem failed due to CSI CRC errors and low frame rate, which is characteristic of a camera ribbon fault. We can proceed directly to proposing the rework.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
